description: How much of the cross-sectional dispersion in realised household loan loss rates across US banks is explained by business mix alone. The institution-level stress test allocates losses pro rata by loan category, which makes business mix the only source of dispersion by construction. This quantifies what that discards.
source: FDIC call reports via the predictive panel, 2001-2024, after the minimum-book rule.
finding: Business mix explains about a tenth of total dispersion and under a third of the FORECASTABLE dispersion. It explains no more under stress: in the 2007-2010 window the mix R-squared is 0.116. A pro rata allocation therefore captures roughly 30 percent of the cross-sectional variation a stress test is trying to rank institutions on.
